title: Rule out half the labels
hook: Find the same target by scanning shuffled labels and halving a sorted list.

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: Use a sorted comparison to eliminate impossible labels and compare observed checks with a target-last shuffled scan.

misconception: A middle comparison can discard half an arbitrary unordered list.
objective: Use a sorted comparison to eliminate impossible labels and compare observed checks with a target-last shuffled scan.

claims.text: A sorted comparison can rule out all labels earlier than the middle when the middle label is less than the target. Unsorted positions do not supply this guarantee.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studySearch.ts: sorted distinct A–J keys; value<target implies all keys at positions≤mid are also<target. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The exercise deliberately puts the largest label last in a shuffled scan list. The scan inspects every label and finds that target on check N. This chosen hard case is not typical search data.
claims.source: shuffledLabels in src/lib/lifehacks/studySearch.ts; reverse the first N−1 distinct letters and leave the largest last. Count is 4..10. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Each sorted-search step compares one midpoint label with the target and shows the remaining inclusive interval. The trace and two counts are actual performed operations.
claims.source: compareLabel in src/lib/lifehacks/studySearch.ts and SearchStage in AlphabetSearchLesson.tsx; midpoint=floor((lo+hi)/2), retained bounds follow the three-way comparison. Scan counts one checked label per item. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: For the disclosed count-10 path, the scan checks 10 labels; the sorted search compares E,J then H,J then I,J then J,J, using 4 checks. Discarded labels fade and are crossed out.
claims.source: Manually reasoned A..J search: lo0,hi9→mid4E→lo5→mid7H→lo8→mid8I→lo9→mid9J. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Only comparisons are counted. Sorting has setup work; this exercise does not measure total organisation time or typical search time.
claims.source: Stated scope of the local fixture. No empirical efficiency guarantee. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The recall requires alphabetical sorting before a midpoint comparison can discard earlier labels.
claims.source: The earlier-position implication requires sortedness; shuffled A..J does not satisfy it. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Only sorted order makes every earlier label smaller than the middle label. Shuffled position supplies no such guarantee.
claims.source: Recall transfer item for this lesson; scenario values are stipulated in the question. The why applies the lesson's own model and limits (see this lesson's idea, limit and formula claims). Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. FC LH-3A (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): verified. No arithmetic. Key 1 only option giving the ordering guarantee; matches c1 (sorted comparison rules out earlier labels). recall.question: A box has shuffled A–J labels. Before a middle comparison can rule out earlier labels, what must you do?
options: Choose the middle of the shuffled box
recall.why: Only sorted order makes every earlier label smaller than the middle label. Shuffled position supplies no such guarantee.
